messages.subject: Change in how reactiveValue works?
parts:
I recently revisited an old Shiny app that needed an update and found that it was broken. The problem boiled down to this:

At the top of my server function I declared a reactiveValue ("globals") with a single element ("path"). During the lifetime of my app this element would be set to the path to a temporary folder containing files that should be zipped together upon download request, so in the downloadHandler there would be a setwd(isolate(globals$path)) before calling zip().

What was now broken was that even though the path element got set at the right time during the life cycle of the app, that change did not propagate to the downloadHandler() content function.

Trying to debug this I switched from using a reactiveValue and instead created an environment to assign a path variable to, but this didn't change a thing. Digging more into it I found that when I was assigning values to the environment it was pointing to another address than when I was reading from it in downloadHandler()

Mockup:
server <- function(input, output, server) {
  globals <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
  
  observe({
    input$action

    assign("path", tempdir(), envir = globals)
  })

  output$download <- downloadHandler(
    filename = "zipfile.zip",
    content = function(file) {
      oldwd <- setwd(globals$path)
      on.exit(setwd(oldwd))
      zip(file, ".")
    }
  )
}

I would assume that globals would consistently point to the same environment, and as my app used to work I believed it used to, but this is no longer the case... Is this a bug or intentional, and how should we in that case pass information on to the downloadHandler?

best

Thomas

messages.subject: Re: Change in how reactiveValue works?
parts:
I recently tried a different hack, just to get things working

I tried to save the value in the package directory using session$token as name (to make sure it was unique to each session) and then read the value in when needed. Surprisingly this didn't work either, and debugging showed that session$token was also different between the observer and downloadHandler. Is this expected? I assumed that session$token would be akin to a unique session id.

If this is not expected it probably points to some problems in how enclosing environments are getting assigned to functions...

best

Thomas

messages.author: 85435c7e2689700c
messages.subject: Re: Change in how reactiveValue works?
parts:
New insight into this issue - though I'm still unsure how to properly fix it

The problem seems to be related to having the server functionality build into a package. My current setup is to define a function "server" and then export a function from my package that internally calls runApp(list(server = server, ui = ...)).

Now when I instead create a server.R file in the 'inst' directory of my package containing shiny::shinyServer(PanVizGenerator:::server) (PanVizGenerator being the name of my package) and change the runApp call to runApp(system.file(package='PanVizGenerator')), everything works fine.

I tried to create a minimal example using the list style runApp functionality but couldn't, which leads me to believe that the problem is only relevant when the server function is being exported from a function and the list style is being used...

For now I can use my workaround, but for the sanity of shiny this should be tracked down and fixed - I fear I can't investigate further though...

best

Thomas

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Change in how reactiveValue works?
parts:
The workaround (for now):
https://github.com/thomasp85/PanVizGenerator/compare/master...jcheng5:patch-1

This is happening because jquery and shiny.js are both getting loaded twice: once explicitly from a <script> tag in your index.html, and once because Shiny itself didn't realize that you had loaded it. Either one of those getting loaded twice is enough to make behavior in the app pretty unpredictable. In this case, we have a not one but TWO sessions initiated by the same page, and the Generate button is talking to one while the Download button is talking to the other.

I think the fact that both JS libraries are getting loaded twice is something we introduced in either Shiny 0.11 or 0.12. We'll get this fixed right away. Fixing it might mean the above workaround should no longer be used--we'll have to see.

Sorry for the inconvenience!

ui = tagList(

)

messages.subject: Re: Change in how reactiveValue works?
parts:
Actually for bootstrap in particular this is better:

bootstrapDependency <- htmltools::htmlDependency("bootstrap", "3.3.1",
        c(
          href = "shared/bootstrap",
          file = system.file("www/shared/bootstrap", package = "shiny")
        ),
        script = c(
          "js/bootstrap.min.js",
          # These shims are necessary for IE 8 compatibility
          "shim/html5shiv.min.js",
          "shim/respond.min.js"
        ),
        stylesheet = if (is.null(theme)) "css/bootstrap.min.css",
        meta = list(viewport = "width=device-width, initial-scale=1")
      )

ui <- htmltools::attachDependencies(includeHTML("www/index.html"), bootstrapDependency)


(Hmmm, ideally we'd let that first big chunk of code be just bootstrapDependency <- shiny::bootstrapDependency. I'll file an issue.)

It's more complicated, but this will prevent bootstrap from getting loaded twice. If you manually put in script/link tags, Shiny doesn't know what you've loaded. The htmlDependency mechanism is a way of declaring CSS/JS dependencies in a way that Shiny can understand.

The workaround (for now):
https://github.com/thomasp85/PanVizGenerator/compare/master...jcheng5:patch-1

This is happening because jquery and shiny.js are both getting loaded twice: once explicitly from a <script> tag in your index.html, and once because Shiny itself didn't realize that you had loaded it. Either one of those getting loaded twice is enough to make behavior in the app pretty unpredictable. In this case, we have a not one but TWO sessions initiated by the same page, and the Generate button is talking to one while the Download button is talking to the other.

I think the fact that both JS libraries are getting loaded twice is something we introduced in either Shiny 0.11 or 0.12. We'll get this fixed right away. Fixing it might mean the above workaround should no longer be used--we'll have to see.

Sorry for the inconvenience!
